Overview table of a cohort

Source: R/cohort-overview.R
describe_cohort.Rd

A preliminary table describing the data set at the start of an analysis: one block of rows per variable with its type, number observed, missing values, summary (overall and by group), a group comparison and a small text histogram of the observed values.

Usage

describe_cohort(
  data,
  vars = NULL,
  by = NULL,
  id_col = NULL,
  blocks = NULL,
  labels = NULL,
  test = TRUE,
  digits = 1,
  spark = TRUE,
  discrete_max = 15,
  missing_warn = 20,
  title = "Cohort overview",
  subtitle = NULL,
  output = c("gt", "data")
)

Arguments

data

A data frame, one row per subject.

vars

Variables to describe (names or tidyselect; default: all but id_col and by).

by

Optional grouping column (e.g. treatment arm).

id_col

Optional identifier column: the subtitle reports the number of unique identifiers and warns about duplicates.

blocks

Optional named list block -> variables, shown as row groups (variables not listed go to "Other variables").

labels

Optional named vector of labels.

test

Compare the groups of by.

digits

Decimals of the summaries.

spark

Add the text-histogram column.

discrete_max

Numeric variables with integer values and at most this number of distinct values are typed "Discrete".

missing_warn

Share of missing values (%) above which the cell is highlighted.

title, subtitle

Title and subtitle (subtitle = NULL: automatic summary of the data set).

output

"gt" (formatted table, needs the gt package) or "data" (the underlying tibble).

Value

A gt_tbl or a tibble (output = "data").

Details

  • Continuous and discrete variables: median [Q1; Q3] and range; text histogram of the observed values (8 bins).

  • Categorical and binary variables: a header row, then one row per level with n (%) of the observed values and a bar proportional to the share.

  • Dates: range.

  • Group comparison (by, test = TRUE): Wilcoxon / Kruskal-Wallis for numeric variables, chi-squared or Fisher (expected counts < 5) for categorical ones; unadjusted p-values, for description only.

  • Variables with more than missing_warn percent missing values are highlighted.

Examples

describe_cohort(cohort_sim, vars = c(AGE, SEX, BMI, NFL_V0, MOCA_V0, FALL_V0),
                by = GROUP, id_col = ID, output = "data")

describe_cohort(cohort_sim, vars = c(AGE, SEX, BMI, NFL_V0, IL6_V0, MOCA_V0, FALL_V0),
                by = GROUP, id_col = ID,
                blocks = list(Demography = c("AGE", "SEX", "BMI"),
                              Biomarkers = c("NFL_V0", "IL6_V0"),
                              Clinical = c("MOCA_V0", "FALL_V0")))

Continuous / discrete: median [Q1; Q3] and range; categorical: n (%) of the observed values. Missing: n (% of subjects). Distribution: histogram of the observed values (8 bins) or share of each level. p: Wilcoxon / Chi², unadjusted (description only).
